## Known biases

The values are FEMA Hazus data redistributed by a third party, not by FEMA; SPHERE does not state which Hazus version or database they were exported from. Every structure, contents and inventory row that FAST (Hazus 4.0 tables) also has is identical, so SPHERE carries the same age and the same limits as the FAST tables (see hazus-flood-functions). SPHERE adds 295 structure and 311 contents rows FAST does not have (ids 705-999 for structures); four structure rows (740-743, source &\#x27;FEMA BCA Toolkit&\#x27;) stop at 16 ft. SPHERE&\#x27;s riverine cross-reference differs from FAST&\#x27;s rule outside whole storey counts 1 to 999 (see assignment\_vs\_fast), so the lab keeps FAST&\#x27;s assignment rule (Yuri&\#x27;s condition, 2026-11-27).

Pandas path: the first matching row in file order (argmax, line 219); no match gives id 0 (line 222). DuckDB path (gather\_damage\_functions): every matching row with weight 1/count (lines 425-448, weight at line 429), so overlapping rows are averaged; buildings with no match get the first cross-reference row with the same first four occupancy letters, ordered by StoriesMin (gather\_missing\_functions, lines 460-488). | read, no claim | <https://github.com/Niyam-Projects/sphere/blob/2967fe660981a185579d6257c3d9df341b695687/packages/flood/src/sphere/flood/default_vulnerability.py> | Line 105 replaces &\#x27;RES3&\#x27; followed by a non-digit with &\#x27;RES3&\#x27;, which leaves the text unchanged. |

No combination present matches more than one cross-reference row. Outside the data the rules also differ for storeys below 1 (SPHERE none, FAST a curve), for RES1 with a fractional storey count (FAST split level 111/112; SPHERE 129 and 111 overlap at 1.5 to 1.6, 107/108 at 2.5) and for RES2 with 2 or more storeys (SPHERE none, FAST 189). So the lab keeps FAST&\#x27;s assignment rule and takes only the values from SPHERE. | read, no claim | <https://github.com/Niyam-Projects/sphere/blob/2967fe660981a185579d6257c3d9df341b695687/packages/data/src/sphere/data/flDmgXRef.csv> | 1900 storeys is most likely a year entered as a storey count; it is a fault in the asset table, not in either rule.
